The Recursive Agents Hackathon
Shack15, San Francisco, CASat, Oct 17 at 9:00 AM – 10:00 PM (PDT)

Build a team of agents you can walk away from.

During the PyTorch Conference in San Francisco, build agents that can take a goal and run with it. Let them make the plan, spin up sub-agents, delegate work, communicate with each other, check their own progress, recover when things break, and keep going.

Get a head start. Crusoe is hosting Field Day the day before the hackathon. You'll join a random team and race to take a model from raw data to production. Friday, Oct 16, 1-5pm. Spots are limited, register here!

Push beyond the one-shot agent into persistent loops that rarely need you involved: agents building teams and handling delegation, memory, and long-running inference that can keep operating after you walk away until the work is complete

Build on Crusoe Managed Inference and put leading open models, including NVIDIA’s Nemotron family, into production on high-performance NVIDIA infrastructure.

Compete to win $25,000 in cash prizes and an NVIDIA RTX 5090.

Note: This event is fully in-person in San Francisco. Teams may have up to four members. All attendees must apply and be approved to attend.

Register

[01]
A new discipline emerges

This past April, Profound introduced Marketing Engineering to the world. Since then, companies like Google have already hired their first Marketing Engineers. Our inaugural hackathon in NYC this June was 5x oversubscribed and brimming with talent. Now, a whole community is thriving.

For the second iteration and our first in San Francisco, this hackathon will push the limits of this new discipline and ask: how do you build systems and agents that let one marketer produce the work of a hundred?

Watch the manifesto

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is this for?

We're seeking aspiring and practicing Marketing Engineers. You're building with agents, experimenting daily to solve real marketing challenges and opportunities, and you have proof of your expertise to show us.

Do I have to use Profound?

No. Every builder gets a Profound instance, but you can ship with whatever stack you want: Cursor, Claude Code, Python, n8n, Replit, your own framework. We keep the playing field clean by giving the Best Profound-native Agent its own prize.

How long is the build window?

From 10 AM to 6 PM PT. You must submit your demo for judging at 6 PM PT, and your workflow must be built on the day of the hackathon, no pre-builds.

Can I bring a teammate?

No teams. The thesis is that one marketing engineer can 10x the productivity of an entire marketing team.

When do I find out if I'm in?

Applications close on at 11:59 pm ET on September 20. Selected builders will hear from us the week of September 21.

What does it cost?

Nothing. Just bring your laptop, your taste, and the willingness to ship something memorable.

Will Profound cover travel costs?

No.

Can I participate remotely?

No, this is an in-person hackathon.

See you on October 3

Applications closed on September 25. Follow along for the announcements.

about this event

Hey Columbia, kick off your fall semester by building something that matters! Secure your spot at the Columbia Hub for the 7th Global AI Hackathon, October 3-4, 2026; a weekend for ambitious builders who want to meet exceptional peers, tackle some of the world's most pressing challenges, and turn bold ideas into real ventures.

Build, prototype, and pitch in just 24 hours, with feedback from mentors and judges whose backgrounds include OpenAI, Meta, Apple, and other leading AI startups.

What's in it for you? $30K+ in cash prizes and API credits across approximately 6-8 AI challenges $200K+ in AI tools and credits available to participating teams An invitation for the top 1% of teams to join our Venture Lab and continue incubating their startups after the hackathon The opportunity to meet and build alongside Columbia students, researchers, engineers, designers, and founders

No idea or team required. Come ready to build. Challenge tracks will be provided.

Agenda October 3 11:00 AM: Local kick-off at Columbia October 4 9:00 AM: Project submission deadline 9:30-10:30 AM: Local pitches at Columbia October 8 Finalists notified October 10 12:00-1:00 PM: Finalist pitches and award ceremony (virtual)

Spots at Columbia are limited and application-only. No walk-ins.

Hosted with the MIT Club of Northern California, MIT Club of Germany, and Hack-Nation. Previous partners and sponsors have included OpenAI, Databricks, Lovable, ElevenLabs, and more. Learn more: hack-nation.ai
